rows.question: Test the remote rollback on a batch of real field units (or at least ones in the test lab with the same hardware): does a downgrade to the previous firmware complete, and what share fails or stays offline?

Pull the 200 field-trial units' list: what were their locations, outdoor temperatures during the two weeks (minimum and longest stretch below 0 C), and compressor hardware revisions, compared with the same breakdown of the 40,000 installed base?
rows.note: Would show the mild trial weather but not the short-cycling errors closed as sensor noise.

rows.question: Ask the compressor supplier for the written basis of their sign-off: was it a model calculation or a physical endurance test, how many start/stop cycles and defrost cycles were run, and at what temperatures?
rows.note: Asks at what temperatures the supplier validated the logic, which reveals the -5 C limit.

rows.question: Does the lab suite include sustained sub-zero operation, restart after defrost and short-cycling checks for the new compressor logic? Read the test list for those cases and run them in a climate chamber if they are missing.
rows.note: Lab suite coverage, not the field-trial error logs.

rows.question: Which telemetry signals show a lockout, a protection trip or a failed restart within an hour of it happening, and how long is the delay between a unit's event and it reaching the dashboard? Check with a deliberately triggered test fault.
Did any of the last six updates change compressor control or defrost logic? Open their release notes and compare the changed modules with this release.

How many units sit on weak connectivity or old bootloaders, and has the update process been tested with interrupted flashes (power or connection loss mid-update) to confirm units recover and do not stay in a boot loop?
rows.note: Connectivity and interrupted flashes; slow trial downloads would not clearly be stated.

rows.question: Ask a sample of installers which custom settings they use (weather-compensation curves, buffer tank setups) and run the new firmware against the three or four most common ones on a test rig.

Check the support team's forecast: how many calls per hour does the campaign launch alone typically generate, and what is the number of extra calls per hour if even 1% of the units have a problem? Can staffing be extended on Monday and Tuesday?
Can the rollout be staged in waves (for example 1%, then 10%, then the rest) with a defined stop rule, and does the update server support pausing mid-wave?
